Below is a complete empirical plan tailored to your data and question. I focus on using quasi-experimental variation from changes in the teacher roster within school-by-grade cells across years, and an explicit test of forecast bias using split-sample IV to purge measurement error in teacher VA.

1. Identification Strategy
- Strategy: Cohort-level difference-in-differences and stacked event study leveraging quasi-experimental shocks to the average predicted teacher quality a cohort faces when teachers enter/exit/switch grades within a school; augmented with split-sample instrumental variables to correct measurement error in predicted value-added.
- Why appropriate:
  - Your data track teachers and cohorts over time, and you already have leave-year-out, teacher-year VA predictions that allow drift. Staff changes induce within-school-by-grade, across-year shifts in average predicted teacher quality (exposure) that are plausibly unrelated to the idiosyncratic quality of a particular incoming cohort, after conditioning on rich cohort composition and fixed effects.
  - Aggregating to the school-by-grade-year (cohort) level circumvents within-cohort sorting of students across classes.
  - A split-sample IV (build two independent out-of-sample VA measures for each teacher-year and use one to instrument the other at the cohort level) yields consistent estimates of the “forecast coefficient” despite measurement error in VA.
  - Dynamic (event-study) patterns around teacher entry/exit provide transparent pre-trend tests and a visual falsification check.

2. Treatment and Control
- Treatment variable:
  - Continuous: Z_sgty = the average predicted teacher value-added (VA) faced by students in school s, grade g, subject y ∈ {math, ELA}, in year t. Construct Z_sgty by weighting each teacher-year’s leave-year-out VA by her share of students taught in that s-g-y-t cell. Build two independent versions using a split-sample jackknife of teachers’ historical data: Z^A and Z^B (fold A and fold B).
- Control group:
  - Cohorts in the same school-by-grade-by-subject with lower (or no) change in predicted average teacher VA across adjacent years; identification comes from within s-g-y comparisons over time, not between schools.
- Treatment timing / event date:
  - Event time is defined at the school-by-grade-by-subject level as the year a material change in Z occurs due to entry/exit/grade-switch by teachers (e.g., |ΔZ| above a pre-specified threshold, such as 0.2 SD).
  - The event study stacks these events and estimates leads/lags of outcomes around the event.
- No RDD is used.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
- A1. As-good-as-random roster shocks within school-by-grade conditional on FE and cohort observables:
  - Changes in Z_sgty are driven by teacher mobility/availability, not by unobserved changes in cohort ability. Plausibility: In large urban districts, grade staffing responds to retirements, transfers, and scheduling needs; we also absorb school-by-grade fixed effects, calendar-year fixed effects, and rich cohort composition (lagged achievement distribution, demographics, parental income mix).
- A2. No differential pre-trends:
  - Absent treatment, cohort mean achievement in an s-g-y cell would have evolved smoothly. Plausibility: We can test this via leads in the event study and by showing Z_sgty is uncorrelated with lagged cohort outcomes/composition changes.
- A3. Exclusion restriction (for IV):
  - Z^B affects cohort outcomes only through true teacher effects; Z^A is measured with classical error independent of Z^B given the split history. Plausibility: Split-sample VA construction yields independent measurement errors across folds by design; exclusion hinges on staffing shocks not triggering other contemporaneous grade-specific interventions.
- A4. Composition stability or adequate control:
  - Any year-to-year changes in the cohort’s observable composition are controlled (lagged scores, FRPL, SPED, ELL, race/ethnicity, gender, parental income bins, match indicator). Plausibility: Administrative data provide these; we will also conduct placebo tests regressing lagged outcomes on Z.
- A5. Limited spillovers/SUTVA at the s-g-y level:
  - A change in teachers for grade g primarily affects outcomes for grade g (subject y) in year t, not other grades. Plausibility: Reasonable for same-year outcomes; we check robustness by including school-by-year fixed effects in an alternative spec that uses within-school-year cross-grade variation.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
- T1. Endogenous staffing to perceived cohort needs (e.g., assigning stronger teachers when incoming lagged scores are low):
  - Mitigation:
    - Include detailed cohort composition controls: full lagged score distribution (e.g., deciles), mean parental income, share SPED/ELL, race/ethnicity, gender, free-lunch, and match indicator.
    - Placebo tests: regress cohort lagged outcomes and demographics on Z to confirm no predictive relationship.
    - Event-study pre-trend checks (leads of Z around entry/exit).
    - Alternative FE: add school-by-grade-specific linear trends to net out slow-moving shifts; and a robustness spec with school-by-year FE (identifies from cross-grade changes within a school-year).
- T2. Measurement error in teacher VA (attenuation of forecast coefficient):
  - Mitigation:
    - Split-sample jackknife for teacher-year VA: construct two independent out-of-sample VA measures per teacher-year; use Z^B as an instrument for Z^A at the cohort level to obtain consistent estimates.
- T3. Within-cohort class sorting correlated with weights used to compute Z (e.g., class sizes/endogenous sectioning):
  - Mitigation:
    - Compute Z using equal weights across teachers within s-g-y-t (robustness).
    - Alternatively, use predetermined weights (prior-year average section shares) as an IV for realized weights.
    - Run the main analysis at the cohort level (Z does not vary within s-g-y-t), limiting exposure to within-cohort sorting.

5. R Code Outline
Notes:
- This is executable skeleton code; adapt variable names to your files.
- We assume two split-sample VA measures per teacher-year: vaA and vaB (constructed from disjoint sets of other years).
- Outcome and lagged scores are standardized within subject-grade-year.

```r
# Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# 1) Load data
# student-level panel: one row per student-subject-school-year
# Required vars: student_id, year, school_id, grade, subject, teacher_id,
# test_std, lag_test_std, sped, ell, race, gender, frpl, matched_tax, parent_income
stu <- fread("student_panel.csv")

# teacher-year VA with split samples (leave-year-out + split across remaining years)
# Required vars: teacher_id, year, subject, vaA, vaB
tva <- fread("teacher_va_split.csv")

# 2) Merge teacher VA to students
setkey(stu, teacher_id, year, subject)
setkey(tva, teacher_id, year, subject)
stu <- tva[stu]  # adds vaA, vaB to student rows

# 3) Construct cohort-level (school x grade x subject x year) exposures and outcomes
# Compute teacher shares within each s-g-subject-year
stu[, sgsy := paste(school_id, grade, subject, year, sep = "_")]
stu[, sgs  := paste(school_id, grade, subject, sep = "_")]

# teacher share weights within cohort
w <- stu[, .(n = .N), by = .(sgsy, teacher_id)]
w[, w_share := n / sum(n), by = sgsy]

# Attach weights back to student-level, then to teacher-level to aggregate Z
setkey(w, sgsy, teacher_id); setkey(stu, sgsy, teacher_id)
stu <- w[stu]

# Equal-weight alternative (for robustness)
w_eq <- stu[, .N, by = .(sgsy, teacher_id)]
w_eq[, w_eq := 1 / .N, by = sgsy]
w_eq <- w_eq[, .(sgsy, teacher_id, w_eq)]

# Cohort-level Z (split-sample A and B), realized-weight baseline
Z <- stu[!is.na(vaA) & !is.na(w_share),
         .(Z_A = sum(w_share * vaA, na.rm = TRUE),
           Z_B = sum(w_share * vaB, na.rm = TRUE)),
         by = .(school_id, grade, subject, year, sgs)]

# Cohort-level outcomes and composition controls
C <- stu[, .(
  y_bar       = mean(test_std, na.rm = TRUE),
  lag_bar     = mean(lag_test_std, na.rm = TRUE),
  inc_bar     = mean(parent_income, na.rm = TRUE),
  p_sped      = mean(sped == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
  p_ell       = mean(ell == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
  p_frpl      = mean(frpl == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
  p_male      = mean(gender == "M", na.rm = TRUE),
  p_match     = mean(matched_tax == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(school_id, grade, subject, year, sgs)]

cohort <- merge(Z, C, by = c("school_id","grade","subject","year","sgs"))

# 4) Main 2SLS at cohort level with school-grade-subject FE and calendar-year FE
# Cluster at school-grade-subject (sgs) level
est_main <- feols(
  y_bar ~ lag_bar + inc_bar + p_sped + p_ell + p_frpl + p_male + p_match | sgs + year + subject ~ Z_A | Z_B,
  data = cohort, cluster = ~ sgs
)
summary(est_main)
# The coefficient on Z_A (2SLS) is the forecast coefficient; test H0: beta = 1
wald(est_main, "fit_Z_A = 1")

# 5) Placebo: do roster shocks predict lagged outcomes?
placebo <- feols(
  lag_bar ~ inc_bar + p_sped + p_ell + p_frpl + p_male + p_match | sgs + year + subject,
  data = merge(cohort, cohort[, .(Z_A, school_id, grade, subject, year, sgs)], by = c("school_id","grade","subject","year","sgs")),
  cluster = ~ sgs
)
# Augment with Z_A on RHS to test for spurious correlation
placebo2 <- feols(
  lag_bar ~ Z_A + inc_bar + p_sped + p_ell + p_frpl + p_male + p_match | sgs + year + subject,
  data = cohort, cluster = ~ sgs
)
summary(placebo2) # Expect coefficient on Z_A ~ 0

# 6) Robustness: equal-weight exposure (no endogenous section sizes)
Z_eq <- merge(stu[, .(school_id, grade, subject, year, sgsy, teacher_id, vaA, vaB)],
              w_eq, by = c("sgsy","teacher_id"), all.x = TRUE)
Z_eq <- Z_eq[, .(Z_A_eq = sum(w_eq * vaA, na.rm = TRUE),
                 Z_B_eq = sum(w_eq * vaB, na.rm = TRUE)),
             by = .(school_id, grade, subject, year, sgs)]
cohort_eq <- merge(C, Z_eq, by = c("school_id","grade","subject","year","sgs"))

est_eq <- feols(
  y_bar ~ lag_bar + inc_bar + p_sped + p_ell + p_frpl + p_male + p_match | sgs + year + subject ~ Z_A_eq | Z_B_eq,
  data = cohort_eq, cluster = ~ sgs
)
summary(est_eq)
wald(est_eq, "fit_Z_A_eq = 1")

# 7) Event study around large shocks in Z
# Define events: years with |ΔZ_A| >= thresh within sgs
cohort[, dZ := Z_A - shift(Z_A), by = sgs]
thresh <- 0.2  # SD units; adjust as needed
events <- cohort[abs(dZ) >= thresh, .(event_year = year), by = sgs]

# Build relative year k = year - event_year, keep window [-3, +3]
evdat <- merge(cohort, events, by = "sgs", allow.cartesian = TRUE)
evdat[, rel := year - event_year]
evdat <- evdat[rel >= -3 & rel <= 3]

# Sunab estimator for dynamic effects on y_bar using Z_A as the “treatment”
# Here we use an indicator for being post-event interacted with rel; or stratify by sign(dZ)
evdat[, post := as.integer(rel >= 0)]
evdat[, sign := factor(sign(dZ), levels = c(-1, 0, 1))]  # optional: stratify by positive vs negative shocks

# Simple stacked event-study (univariate leads/lags of rel)
for (k in setdiff(-3:3, -1)) {  # omit rel = -1 as base
  evdat[, paste0("L", k) := as.integer(rel == k)]
}
fml_ev <- as.formula(paste0("y_bar ~ ", paste(paste0("L", setdiff(-3:3, -1)), collapse = " + "),
                            " + lag_bar + inc_bar + p_sped + p_ell + p_frpl + p_male + p_match | sgs + year + subject"))
est_ev <- feols(fml_ev, data = evdat, cluster = ~ sgs)
summary(est_ev)
# Plot coefficients on leads/lags to inspect pre-trends vs impact at rel=0/+1

# 8) Optional: Student-level 2SLS using cohort Z as instrument for own teacher VA
# This focuses on the mapping from predicted teacher VA to individual outcomes and provides another check.
# Endogenous regressor: student’s teacher vaA; IV: cohort Z_B
stu_cohortZ <- merge(stu, Z[, .(school_id, grade, subject, year, Z_B)], by = c("school_id","grade","subject","year"))
est_indiv <- feols(
  test_std ~ lag_test_std + sped + ell + frpl + gender + race + parent_income + matched_tax | sgs + year + subject ~ vaA | Z_B,
  data = stu_cohortZ, cluster = ~ sgs
)
summary(est_indiv)
```

6. Expected Results
- Direction: If teacher VA measures are unbiased forecasts of causal effects, a one-unit increase in cohort exposure to predicted teacher VA should raise cohort mean test scores by one unit (beta ≈ 1). Pre-trend coefficients should be near zero; placebo regressions of lagged outcomes on Z should yield nulls.
- Magnitude: I expect an estimated forecast coefficient close to 1 (e.g., 0.9–1.1 after IV correction), with OLS attenuated below 1 due to measurement error. Event-study should show an on-impact jump at event time and flat pre-trends.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
- C1: As-good-as-random variation in staffing within school-by-grade after FE/controls — 1
- C2: No differential pre-trends (validated by event-study leads/placebos) — 1
- C3: Strong first stage (substantial variation in Z from roster changes; F-stat >> 10) — 1
- C4: Exclusion restriction (no concurrent grade-specific interventions triggered by staffing changes) — 0
- C5: Limited spillovers/SUTVA at the s-g-y level (no cross-grade contamination within-year) — 0

Notes:
- The split-sample construction of VA (vaA, vaB) must use disjoint sets of teacher-years excluding year t to ensure independent measurement errors. If teacher-year histories are short, use k-fold cross-fitting.
- Always re-standardize test scores within subject-grade-year so VA and outcomes are on the same scale.
